PCOP.title: Black copied White's move. Good idea? #shorts
PCOP.desc:
The Petrov Defense copycat: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4? 4.Qe2 Nf6?? 5.Nc6+, a discovered check from the queen, and the knight takes the queen on d8. After 4.Qe2 Black has to play 4...Qe7.

Would you have copied?

#chess #chesstraps #petrovdefense

PCOP.ig:
Black just copied White's move. Is that a good idea? Would you have copied?

DAMI.title: White gave up a knight. Should Black take it? #shorts
DAMI.desc:
The Damiano Defense: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f6? 3.Nxe5! fxe5? 4.Qh5+ g6 5.Qxe5+ Qe7 6.Qxh8. The knight isn't free, and the real mistake was 2...f6. After 3.Nxe5 Black should play 3...Qe7.

Would you have taken it?

#chess #chesstraps #chessopenings
DAMI.tags: chess, chess shorts, damiano defense, chess traps, fork, chess openings, chess for beginners, chess tips
DAMI.ig:
White just gave up a knight for a pawn. Should Black take it? Would you have taken it?

#chess #chesstraps #chessopenings #chesstips #chessforbeginners

QGAB.title: Black grabbed a pawn. Can he keep it? #shorts
QGAB.desc:
Queen's Gambit Accepted: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 b5? 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5?? 6.Qf3, and the rook on a8 is attacked along the long diagonal. If 6...Nc6, then 7.Qxc6+. Trying to keep the extra pawn costs a whole piece.

Did you know this one?

#chess #queensgambit #chesstraps
QGAB.tags: chess, chess shorts, queens gambit, queens gambit accepted, chess traps, chess openings, long diagonal, chess for beginners
QGAB.ig:
Black just grabbed a pawn. Can he hold on to it? Did you know this one?

#chess #queensgambit #chesstraps #chessopenings #chesstips

LTRP.title: This bishop looks free. Is it? #shorts
LTRP.desc:
The Lasker trap in the Albin Countergambit: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5 3.dxe5 d4 4.e3? Bb4+ 5.Bd2 dxe3 6.Bxb4?? exf2+ 7.Ke2 fxg1=N+! 8.Rxg1 Bg4+ and the white queen falls. The pawn becomes a knight because a knight gives check.

Would you have taken the bishop?

#chess #chesstraps #underpromotion
LTRP.tags: chess, chess shorts, lasker trap, albin countergambit, underpromotion, chess traps, chess openings, queens gambit
LTRP.ig:
White can take this bishop for free. Is it really free? Would you have taken the bishop?

#chess #chesstraps #underpromotion #chessopenings #chesstips

KIEN.title: White can win a bishop. Should he take it? #shorts
KIEN.desc:
The Kieninger trap in the Budapest Gambit: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e5 3.dxe5 Ng4 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.Bf4 Bb4+ 6.Nbd2 Qe7 7.a3 Ngxe5 8.axb4?? Nd3#. The king is boxed in by his own pieces, and the pawn on e2 can't take because the queen on e7 pins it.

Would you have grabbed it?

#chess #chesstraps #budapestgambit
KIEN.tags: chess, chess shorts, kieninger trap, budapest gambit, smothered mate, chess traps, chess openings, pin
KIEN.ig:
White can win a whole bishop here. Should he take it? Would you have grabbed it?

#chess #chesstraps #budapestgambit #checkmate #chessopenings

CKNM.title: Black brought out a knight. What's wrong? #shorts
CKNM.desc:
The Caro-Kann trap: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nd7 5.Qe2 Ngf6?? 6.Nd6#. The pawn on e7 is pinned by the queen on e2, so nothing can take the knight. 5...Ndf6 was the move.

Did you see it?

#chess #carokann #chesstraps
CKNM.tags: chess, chess shorts, caro kann, smothered mate, chess traps, chess openings, checkmate in six, pin
CKNM.ig:
Black just brought out a knight. Can you see what's wrong? Did you see it?

OPRA.title: Why would Morphy give away his queen? #shorts
OPRA.desc:
The Opera Game, Paris 1858: Paul Morphy against the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard, played at the opera. 16.Qb8+!! Nxb8 17.Rd8#. The queen drags the knight off the d-file, and the rook mates with the bishop on g5 covering d8.

Did you know this game?

#chess #morphy #operagame
OPRA.tags: chess, chess shorts, opera game, paul morphy, queen sacrifice, famous chess games, chess history, checkmate
OPRA.ig:
Morphy is about to give away his queen with check. Why would he? Did you know this game?

#chess #morphy #operagame #chesshistory #queensacrifice

IMMO.title: Both rooks gone, the queen next. Who wins? #shorts
IMMO.desc:
The Immortal Game, London 1851: Adolf Anderssen against Lionel Kieseritzky. 18.Bd6!! Bxg1 19.e5 Qxa1+ 20.Ke2 Na6 21.Nxg7+ Kd8 22.Qf6+!! Nxf6 23.Be7#. White mates with two knights and a bishop.

Did you know this game?

#chess #immortalgame #chesshistory
IMMO.tags: chess, chess shorts, immortal game, anderssen, kieseritzky, famous chess games, chess history, sacrifice
IMMO.ig:
White has given away both rooks, and now he gives away his queen. Who wins? Did you know this game?

#chess #immortalgame #chesshistory #famouschessgames #checkmate

EVGR.title: White gives away his queen. Can you see why? #shorts
EVGR.desc:
The Evergreen Game, Berlin 1852: Adolf Anderssen against Jean Dufresne. 20.Rxe7+ Nxe7 21.Qxd7+!! Kxd7 22.Bf5++ (double check) Ke8 23.Bd7+ Kf8 24.Bxe7#.

Did you know this game?

#chess #evergreengame #chesshistory
EVGR.tags: chess, chess shorts, evergreen game, anderssen, double check, famous chess games, chess history, queen sacrifice
EVGR.ig:
White gives away his queen with check here. Can you see why? Did you know this game?

#chess #evergreengame #chesshistory #doublecheck #queensacrifice

LSKT.title: The king takes the queen. Where does he end up? #shorts
LSKT.desc:
Edward Lasker vs George Thomas, London 1912: 11.Qxh7+!! Kxh7 12.Nxf6+ Kh6 13.Neg4+ Kg5 14.h4+ Kf4 15.g3+ Kf3 16.Be2+ Kg2 17.Rh2+ Kg1 18.Kd2#. The black king walks all the way to White's first row.

Did you know this game?

#chess #kinghunt #chesshistory
LSKT.tags: chess, chess shorts, king hunt, edward lasker, famous chess games, chess history, queen sacrifice, checkmate
LSKT.ig:
White gives away his queen, and the black king takes it. Where does that king end up? Did you know this game?

#chess #kinghunt #chesshistory #famouschessgames #checkmate

GOLD.title: Why put the queen where she can be taken 3 ways? #shorts
GOLD.desc:
Levitsky vs Marshall, Breslau 1912: 23...Qg3!! If 24.hxg3 Ne2#. If 24.fxg3 Ne2+ 25.Kh1 Rxf1#. If 24.Qxg3 Ne2+ 25.Kh1 Nxg3+ 26.Kg1 Nxf1, and Black stays a piece up. Levitsky resigned. The story of the gold coins is a legend.

Did you know this move?

#chess #marshall #chesshistory
GOLD.tags: chess, chess shorts, gold coins game, frank marshall, queen sacrifice, famous chess games, chess history, chess tactics
GOLD.ig:
Marshall puts his queen where White can take her three different ways. Why? Did you know this move?

#chess #marshall #chesshistory #queensacrifice #chesstactics

DBLU.title: A computer gave up a knight vs the champion. Good idea? #shorts
DBLU.desc:
Deep Blue vs Garry Kasparov, New York 1997, game 6: 8.Nxe6! Qe7 9.O-O fxe6 10.Bg6+ Kd8, and Black's king never got out. Kasparov resigned after 19 moves, and Deep Blue won the match 3.5 to 2.5.

Would you have taken the knight?

#chess #deepblue #kasparov
DBLU.tags: chess, chess shorts, deep blue, kasparov, computer chess, famous chess games, chess history, caro kann
DBLU.ig:
A computer gives up a knight against the world champion on move eight. Good idea? Would you have taken the knight?

#chess #deepblue #kasparov #chesshistory #computerchess

GOTC.title: A 13-year-old gives up his queen. Mistake? #shorts
GOTC.desc:
The Game of the Century, New York 1956: Donald Byrne vs Bobby Fischer. 17...Be6!! 18.Bxb6 Bxc4+ 19.Kg1 Ne2+ 20.Kf1 Nxd4+ 21.Kg1 Ne2+ 22.Kf1 Nc3+ 23.Kg1 axb6, and Fischer mated 24 moves later with 41...Rc2#.

Did you know this game?

#chess #bobbyfischer #chesshistory
GOTC.tags: chess, chess shorts, game of the century, bobby fischer, donald byrne, queen sacrifice, famous chess games, chess history
GOTC.ig:
A thirteen-year-old gives up his queen in one of the most famous games ever. Was it a mistake? Did you know this game?

#chess #bobbyfischer #chesshistory #gameofthecentury #queensacrifice

PHIL.title: A pawn down in a rook endgame. Can Black save it? #shorts
PHIL.desc:
The Philidor position: white king d5, rook a7, pawn e5; black king e8, rook h8, Black to move. 1...Rf8? 2.Ra8+ Kd7 3.e6+ Kc7 4.Rxf8 loses. 1...Rh6! keeps the white king off the sixth row, and after 2.e6 Rh1 the rook checks from behind: a draw. Checked with an endgame tablebase.

Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #rookendgame
PHIL.tags: chess, chess shorts, philidor position, rook endgame, chess endgames, drawing technique, chess tips, chess for beginners
PHIL.ig:
Black is a pawn down in a rook endgame. Can he save it? Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #rookendgame #chessendgames #chesstips

WBSH.title: A bishop and a pawn up. Is it a win? #shorts
WBSH.desc:
The wrong bishop: with a rook pawn, the bishop must control the corner square. Dark bishop and a8 pawn: 1.Kb5 Ka7 2.a6 Ka8 3.Kb6 is stalemate, a draw. Light bishop: 1.Bd3 Ka7 2.a6 Kb8 3.Kb6 Ka8 4.Bb1 Kb8 5.a7+ Ka8 6.Be4#. Checked with an endgame tablebase.

Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #stalemate
WBSH.tags: chess, chess shorts, wrong bishop, rook pawn, chess endgames, stalemate, chess tips, chess for beginners
WBSH.ig:
White is a bishop and a pawn up. Is that a win? Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #stalemate #chessendgames #chesstips

QVP7.title: A queen vs one pawn. Always a win? #shorts
QVP7.desc:
Queen against a pawn on the seventh. Against a d-pawn the queen checks until the king blocks his own pawn, and the white king walks in: a win. Against a c-pawn (or an a-pawn) the king hides in the corner instead, and Qxc2 is stalemate. With the white king far away, it is a draw. Checked with an endgame tablebase.

Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #stalemate
QVP7.tags: chess, chess shorts, queen vs pawn, stalemate trick, chess endgames, chess tips, chess for beginners, endgame theory
QVP7.ig:
A queen against one little pawn. Is that always a win? Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #stalemate #chessendgames #chesstips

BRKT.title: Three pawns vs three. Can White make a queen? #shorts
BRKT.desc:
The pawn breakthrough: white pawns a5 b5 c5, black pawns a7 b7 c7, kings far away. 1.b6! axb6 2.c6! bxc6 3.a6 and the pawn queens. If 1...cxb6 2.a6! bxa6 3.c6, the same.

Did you know this trick?

#chess #endgame #pawnbreakthrough
BRKT.tags: chess, chess shorts, pawn breakthrough, pawn endgame, chess endgames, chess tricks, chess tips, chess for beginners
BRKT.ig:
Three pawns against three. Can White make a queen? Did you know this trick?

#chess #endgame #pawnbreakthrough #chessendgames #chesstips

SAAV.title: This pawn is about to promote. Is it a win? #shorts
SAAV.desc:
The Saavedra position (1895): 1.c7 Rd6+ 2.Kb5 Rd5+ 3.Kb4 Rd4+ 4.Kb3 Rd3+ 5.Kc2 Rd4! 6.c8=R! (6.c8=Q? Rc4+ 7.Qxc4 is stalemate) 6...Ra4 7.Kb3, and Black loses the rook or gets mated on c1.

Did you know this one?

#chess #saavedra #underpromotion

SAAV.ig:
This pawn is about to become a queen. Is it a win? Did you know this one?

#chess #saavedra #underpromotion #chessendgames #stalemate

PINC.title: Can the black king take this queen? #shorts
PINC.desc:
No. The bishop on e5 is pinned by the rook on e8, but a pinned piece still guards the squares it sees, and a king can never step onto a guarded square. Qxg7 is checkmate.

Did you know this rule?

#chess #chessrules #checkmate
PINC.tags: chess, chess shorts, pin, chess rules, checkmate, chess tips, chess for beginners, chess facts
PINC.ig:
Can the black king take this queen? Did you know this rule?

#chess #chessrules #checkmate #chesstips #chessforbeginners

TWNK.title: Two knights vs a lone king. Can they force mate? #shorts
TWNK.desc:
No. With two knights you can only mate if the defender helps: after 1.Ne7+ Kh8?? 2.Nf7# is mate, but 1...Kf8 and there is no mate. King and two knights against a king is a draw with correct defense.

Did you know this one?

#chess #endgame #checkmate

TWNK.ig:
